articles.title: What Is an LLM? Large Language Models Explained Plainly
articles.excerpt: LLM stands for large language model. It is software trained on a very large amount of text to do one thing: given some text, predict what comes next. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama and DeepSeek are la…
articles.body: LLM stands for large language model. It is software trained on a very large amount of text to do one thing: given some text, predict what comes next. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama and DeepSeek are large language models, or products built on top of one. Predicting the next words sounds small. Done well enough, it lets a program read a customer email, follow a written policy, and write a reply in the customer's language. This page explains how that works, where it stops working, and what a business needs around the model to get real work out of it. What the three words mean Large: the model has billions of internal settings, called parameters, and it was trained on a large share of the public text that exists in books, websites and code. Language: it works in text.

articles.title: What is prompt engineering? What works in production
articles.excerpt: Prompt engineering is the practice of structuring the instructions, context, and output format you send to a large language model so it produces reliable results for a specific task. In everyday work,…
articles.body: Prompt engineering is the practice of structuring the instructions, context, and output format you send to a large language model so it produces reliable results for a specific task. In everyday work, the biggest gains rarely come from clever phrasing; they come from giving the model clean, relevant facts and removing conflicting rules. Distilling messy threads and raw order payloads into concise, structured facts fixes more errors than stacking extra rules into a long prompt. The four parts of a production prompt A prompt inside a live business system is not a single sentence typed into a chat box. It has four distinct layers: Role and scope: what job this step owns and what it must not decide.

articles.title: Notification is not disclosure: chemical risk notices neighbours can actually use
articles.excerpt: Most sites that store hazardous chemicals can produce a notification document on request. Very few can show that a single neighbour read it and knew what to do. That gap — between a file that satisfie…
articles.body: Most sites that store hazardous chemicals can produce a notification document on request. Very few can show that a single neighbour read it and knew what to do. That gap — between a file that satisfies an inspector and a message that works at three in the morning — is where community risk communication fails. Under Korean regulation (Chemical Substances Control Act, 화학물질관리법, Article 23-3), a site that receives a compliance notice for its chemical accident prevention plan must tell nearby residents three things: the hazard of the substances handled, the potential impact of an accident on air, water, groundwater, soil and the surrounding environment, and the early-warning method with evacuation actions.

articles.excerpt: Originally published on Mindima Learn. In short: The best apps for memory improvement are built on techniques with strong evidence: practising recall of the specific things you want to remember, space…
articles.body: Originally published on Mindima Learn . In short: The best apps for memory improvement are built on techniques with strong evidence: practising recall of the specific things you want to remember, spaced out over days, often with a mnemonic strategy such as the memory palace. Research shows that people get better at the tasks they practise, but there is little evidence that generic brain games carry over to everyday memory. No app has been shown to give you a better memory in general. Some apps, though, are built around methods that decades of memory research support, and you can learn to tell those apart from the rest. This guide covers what the studies show, what to look for, and what to skip. What makes an app good for memory improvement?

articles.title: SpaceX Starship debris becomes art in Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' (video, photos)
articles.excerpt: Explore Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' Monuments in marble, Ejecta prints, Launch Sequence sculptures and interactive Crowded Sky at Heft Gallery in New York City.
articles.body: When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Some of that material now hangs on a gallery wall in New York City, embedded in artist Ashley Zelinskie's print of the very explosion it survived. Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. "I think you might want these," Zelinskie recalled one friend telling her. She did. The Brooklyn-based artist ground the fragments into dust and worked them into the print. Ashley Zelinskie incorporated dust from recovered SpaceX Starship heat-shield tiles into this print of the vehicle breaking apart over Turks and Caicos.

articles.title: Pakistani astronaut becomes 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station (photos)
articles.excerpt: Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first international astronaut to visit China's Tiangong space station today (Nov. 25), when he and his Shenzhou-24 crewmates docked with the outpost.
articles.body: For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station. That pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25). "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an update today (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!" Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 .
